content.text:
View A represents four spots. The lower spot is a yellow circle and is currently dominant and readily available. The upper spot looks blue and is most likely a square but is currently barely attended and only weakly recoverable. The right spot looks green and is a triangle but is also scarcely attended. The left spot has a flat, ambiguous color and shape and is essentially unavailable. Predicted effects of commands show little control over where attention goes: most commands in this model drive attention to the right spot, so attempting to redirect would typically shift availability away from the currently dominant lower item toward the right item, leaving the others still poorly available.

View B also contains four spots. The lower spot is a blue triangle and is currently dominant and highly available. The upper spot is red and likely a square but is only weakly attended. The left spot is green and a cross with moderate recoverability despite low current selection; the right spot is yellow and a circle but currently unattended. In contrast to A, commands in view B reliably move attention to the named location, so redirecting attention to any given spot will make that spot the most available.
